cells.tense: You can feel how many directions this could go and you still get to pick.
cells.act: work the pattern through to its logic
cells.ask: Follow one feeling you carry toward someone out to where it actually leads — what would follow, who ends up where. Take the chain to its last link, set that down, and stop. Leave it alone after.
cells.core:
A lot is available right now, and it isn't confusion. It's the whole harvest — every direction the heart could take, all of it warm. You can hold that much without being torn apart by it. Something between you and another person is at the point where it either changes or it stops, and you don't have to know yet which of the many next things it becomes. The pull is real, and so is the clearing waiting on it.

Do the arithmetic on a single feeling. Follow it forward to where it actually goes — not how it feels about itself, but what would follow and who'd be standing where afterward. Take the chain of it to the last link and set that down in writing, not speech. A good part of the pull can't survive the sum. What can, you'll already have settled.
cells.sheetLine: You can hold every direction and still pick one.
cells.verb: gathering every feeling the heart could want and letting most of them go
cells.place: at the clearing where one thing has to end before the next can start

cells.tense: The ending gets rehearsed in you before anyone has decided it.
cells.ask: Something in your life already sits in a different shape than it did. Say what it is now in one plain sentence and leave it that way for the week, without adjusting it back.
cells.core:
You can feel all the ways this could end and part of you is already braced for it. Goodbyes get made before the facts arrive. The pull runs hot: it sees every possible feeling and calls each one soon. Meanwhile, something has already ended cleanly or shifted into another shape, and that part isn't the problem — you just haven't let it stay. Reopening what has settled is where the strain lives.

Take one change from the last few months — how your evenings go, a distance between you and someone, a habit that fell away — and say what it is now and nothing else. Not what it was, not whether it was right. Let the shape hold for a week without you adjusting it. The next thing can wait until the ground stops shifting under it.

cells.tense: You stepped back from the feeling and you have not moved since.
cells.act: let the mind rest instead of working the problem
cells.ask: Sit somewhere plain and give the question a rest — no figuring, no re-deciding, no rehearsing what you'd say. Nothing to solve. When you notice the mind working it again, stop.
cells.core:
Whatever was possible here, you've stepped back from it — from the feeling, from the crowd of directions. Something ended and you keep your hand on it, turning over what it should have been. The pull is still there. You've stopped answering, and the not-answering reads to you as care.

Nothing here needs settling — not whose fault it was, not what it meant, not whether staying was ever an option. Put the question somewhere you can't reach it and be still with it. Not a verdict, not a plan. Just quiet, on purpose, and short. The ending doesn't need your supervision to stay ended.
cells.sheetLine: You've stopped answering, and you're still there.

cells.tense: You are doing the ending and your account of it leaves you out.
cells.act: cut through the story to what actually follows
cells.ask: Find a sentence you keep repeating about why this ended — the meaning version, not the fact. Strip it to the bare fact, say that fact once, then name what follows from it. Nothing more.
cells.core:
Something in you decides what ends here and what stays, and has been deciding for some time. Your account of it doesn't have that in it. You describe the loss as though it arrived from outside, and meanwhile you keep walking off the edges of what's already over. The outcomes weren't accidents. There's a hand on the tiller, and you haven't signed for it — the part of you doing the clearing is good at it and unnamed in your own story.

Take one sentence you keep repeating about why this ended — the meaning version, not the fact. Strip it to the bare fact underneath. Then set down what follows from that fact, three lines, the way you'd reason through anything. Your hand chose the ending. This says it back to you in your own words, on the record.
cells.sheetLine: You chose the ending and your story skips your part.

attempts.check: The weakest claim is that the pull toward possible feelings is *currently* being ended or cleared — the record supports Allure landing in Transformation, but not that the person has already started closing anything. A reader could reasonably say the endings are someone else's or that nothing is ending at all yet, only pull. The four asks survive being wrong: each is a small move the person can do whether or not the read is right, and none depends on the endings being theirs. The sentence that serves me more than them is any phrasing that assumes the loss is already complete — 'what's already over' — so I've kept the endings as something the person is deciding about, not something done to them.
